faq.q: What do I say in an apology note?
faq.a: Say who it is for, what you did, that you are sorry, that you understand how they feel, how you will fix it, and sign your name.
asks: How do I write a sorry letter?

faq.q: How do I show I understand in a sorry note?
faq.a: Name their feeling: I know you were upset, or: I know that pot was special to you. It shows you thought about them, not just you.
asks: Tell me about the Show you understand

faq.q: What can I offer in an apology note?
faq.a: Offer to fix or replace it, help out, or do something kind, like: I can help you plant new flowers.
asks: Tell me about the Offer to fix it

faq.q: Is a sorry note better than saying sorry?
faq.a: Both are good. A note helps when you feel shy, or when you want time to choose your words. Saying sorry in person as well is even better.
asks: Should I write or say sorry?

faq.q: What if I am too scared to give the note?
faq.a: Ask a parent or trusted adult to come with you. Being honest is hard but people usually respect it a lot.
asks: I am scared to say sorry

facts: A 2016 study by Roy Lewicki found that taking responsibility and offering to repair the harm are the most important parts of an apology.
Writing an apology lets you think carefully about your words before sharing them.
